item.title: Jennifer's Body (2009) — Fri Oct 30, 7:00 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description:
Perfect start to the Halloween Weekend!
Megan Fox stars in this horror-comedy about a sexy high school cheerleader who develops an insatiable appetite for her male classmates after she’s possessed by a hungry demon.
Initially a box office flop in 2009, years later fans and critics have re-evaluated the film as a smart and biting satire on female friendship, trauma, and the way society treats young women — turning it into a beloved horror staple and a celebrated queer feminist masterpiece.
Writer: Diablo Cody Director: Karyn Kusama Cast: Megan Fox, Amanda Seyfried, Johnny Simmons, J.K. Simmons, Amy Sedaris, Adam Brody
LENGTH: 1hr 45mins FORMAT: DCP RATED: R
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Oct 31 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Nov 2 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Nov 2 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Preventing Campus Violence: Building Community Safety and Accountability — Tue Nov 3, 6:00 PM — Woodburn Hall
item.description:
Middle Way House Club at Indiana University is hosting a discussion about the culture of sexual violence on campus and about skills that build safety and accountability in our community. We want to hold compassion and care together as emotions around rape culture continue to rise. We know as our institutions around us continue to fail and not provide safety, we have to keep our own community safe. During this event we will build the skills of accountability, safety planning, bystander intervention and more. Join us Tuesday the 3rd at 6:00 pm!
Hosted by: Middle Way House Club at IU
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12940901

From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Nov 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Fri Nov 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: Embedded Accessible Educational Services (AES) — Fri Nov 6, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
At the LGBTQ+ Culture Center, we want every student to have the resources they need to thrive. Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes, and many are not visible to others. Accessible Educational Services (AES) partners with students to provide accommodations, support services, and tools that help create equal access and opportunity at IU. Kade Padgett, M.A., an AES Access Coordinator, is available at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center every Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. during drop-in advising hours. item.title: Union Board Out & About Presents: Let's Go Caving! — Fri Nov 6, 12:00 PM — IMU Biddle Hotel Lobby
item.description:
Union Board’s Out & About committee is heading underground, and we’re taking 50 students with us to Marengo Cave, completely free of charge! Meet at the IMU Biddle Hotel Lobby by 12:00 PM, where we'll drive everyone down to Marengo Cave in southern Indiana. Once there, you’ll take the Dripstone Tour, a guided one-mile walk through the cave that takes about an hour. Snacks and bottled water provided. When the tour wraps up, we’ll bring you back to the IMU by around 5:30 PM. No caving experience needed. Just bring a jacket, since it stays cool underground all year. item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Nov 6, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Nov 6, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Animal Hour / Dive Deeper — Fri Nov 6, 3:00 PM — Wonderlab
item.description:
November Theme: Technology Day: Friday Times 3 - 4pm Recommended for: All ages Event Price Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Get closer to the wild side with Animal Hour and Dive Deeper! These weekly programs let you chat with WonderLab's animal experts, discover what it takes to care for creatures from around the globe, and meet snakes, lizards, insects, arachnids, and more-up close and out of their habitats. Animal Hour takes place on most Fridays, while Dive Deeper happens on the last Friday of each month at WonderLab's stunning coral reef aquarium. Type of Activities Animal Hour: Meet our animal ambassadors. Observe the tools we use to care for our animal ambassadors. Type of Activities Dive Deeper: Tour the reef system and learn the mechanics behind how it functions.
